title: Router context is always app=none; online check stale and blocking
detail: self._ctx is initialised once and never updated (no write to _ctx anywhere), so every route sees app=none focused=none selection=no last_action=none. Training spends 3,000 G3 context-pair items + follow-up items on exactly these fields ('cut this' in Premiere -> premiere_command; 'a bit more' after set_volume -> change_volume); at runtime they can never fire. online= comes from decision._online_ok: a blocking 0.5 s TCP connect to 8.8.8.8 inside route() on the asyncio loop, cached 30 s -> right after 'turn off Wi-Fi' the router still believes online=yes for up to 30 s, and on a bad venue network one instant command per 30 s pays +500 ms. Also `--tau` is parsed (cli.py:158) but never passed to Orchestrator.
evidence: grep '_ctx\[' orchestrator.py@b438799 -> none; decision.py:116-121,217-221; cli.py:56 `Orchestrator(server, Catalog.load(), Tracer(), engine=engine)` without tau.
fix: Have the app include `app` (frontmost localizedName) and `focused` summary in the utterance frame (AGENTS.md contract addition, ~0 ms; it already knows NSWorkspace.frontmostApplication) and set _ctx from it; set _ctx['last_action'] = 'set_volume level=30' after each successful skill; after a wifi skill set online explicitly; move the reachability probe to a background task (SCNetworkReachability-equivalent on the Swift side is better). Pass tau through.

title: Partials dropped; ARGS decode always serial after release
detail: The app sends partial utterances every 450 ms (VoiceController.swift:166-185) but the server ignores non-final frames, so route+args start only after release + 60 ms tail + full-clip Parakeet re-transcribe. Then orchestrator calls engine.args for every skill, including zero-arg skills (sleep_display, battery_status, todays_agenda, copy_selection) and bool/enum ones, as up-to-32-token greedy decode with a per-token full Python round trip. Instant-command budget today (estimates, unmeasured end-to-end): STT final ~? + route ~15-40 ms + args ~8-20 tokens x ~10-20 ms = 80-400 ms + skill ms; route/args run synchronously on the event loop. The route+args part can be ~0 on the critical path.
evidence: server.py@b438799:104 `if msg.get("final"):`; orchestrator.py:165 unconditional `self.engine.args(label, ...)`; decision.py:342 `for _ in range(32)` with np.argmax per step.
fix: On each partial: run route (+args if p_top>=tau) in a worker thread keyed by normalized text; on final, if normalize(final)==normalize(last speculated), execute the cached decision immediately. Skip args when the skill has no args; for single bool/enum args use one more choice question (one forward pass) instead of decode. Measure and trace release->skill_start ms as the headline number vs HobbyLM's 0.26 s.

title: Executor drops expects and ends batches at scripts; prompt promises otherwise
detail: (a) `if op == "script": return await self._script(a)` returns after the first script, silently skipping later actions and reporting ok. (b) _script builds params {op,lang,code} and _skill sends {name,args}: any `expect` the planner attached to a script/skill is discarded, so rule 3 and design rule 'every consequential action carries an expect' are unenforced on the two most-recommended paths (rule 1 + Numbers rule 8). (c) `done` is said verbatim with no verification, yet prompt example 3 emits `done` in the same batch as the write script, before any observation (contradicts prompt rule 4 and AGENTS 'DONE is verified by the harness'). (d) Prompt says click x,y are 0-1000 image coords; Act.swift:272-281 clicks them as global points and the brain does no conversion (and has no screenshot path at all) -> every pixel click lands in the top-left 1000x1000 pt. (e) Prompt lists `script applescript|jxa`; AGENTS.md/dsl.py also allow shell.
evidence: orchestrator.py@b438799:287,328; Act.swift@b438799:272-281 `let p = CGPoint(x: x, y: y)`; planner_system.md@cdae5d9:20,23,66-71.
fix: script: `r = await self._script(a); if r != 'ok': return r; continue`; pass a.get('expect') into the script act params and run `verify {expect}` after a skill when present; on `done` call verify on the last expect (or re-observe and hand it to the planner once) before saying success; convert click coords brain-side using the screenshot's {origin, width, height, scale}; fix example 3 to end with `expect`/no done and let the next turn emit done.

title: No benchmark harness exists for HobbyLM, DeskMind, JevBench or typed decisions
detail: bench/ contains only speed_lab.py (synthetic shapes) and run_when_ready.sh; there is no /v1/systemone shim, no HobbyLM 125-task runner, no DeskMind Bench (13 tasks) runner, no JevBench or typed-decisions adapter. 'Beat them on their own benchmarks' is the headline claim and needs >= a day of harness work. Fairness notes: HobbyLM's 0.26 s is median decision latency with a fixed action vocabulary and no vision, so compare our route p50 (warm cache, same utterances) not end-to-end; its 72% is live task success on 125 tasks -> we must run all 125 live on the Mac (not a subset) and report failures. DeskMind Bench is 13 live macOS tasks scored by success -> needs the planner (architect-1). SPEC 1.5 dedups against HobbyLM data/frozen tests (good), but evals/route_v1.jsonl is hand-written and should not be reported as a public number.
evidence: git ls-tree origin/main bench/ -> run_when_ready.sh, speed_lab.py; git grep -i 'systemone|hobbylm|deskmind bench|jevbench' -- ml bench evals -> only a model id in speed_lab.py docstring.
fix: Build in this order: (1) brain HTTP endpoint POST /v1/systemone {state, questions} -> distributions (wraps DecisionEngine.route) so HobbyLM's/typed-decisions scripts can call us unchanged (~2 h); (2) HobbyLM task adapter mapping their fixed vocab -> our skills, run all 125 live, log per-task (~3 h); (3) DeskMind Bench runner once planner exists. Publish latency with identical measurement points (first token/decision after text available).

detail: calc.result(text) runs before self.engine routing for every final utterance. This would break the Numbers finance demo ('highlight rows 2-10' -> 'You said 2-10 is -8') and browser and Premiere commands with numbers, presenting a wrong answer as success. title: First planner action waits for the second action line to decode
detail: AGENTS: start the first action while the planner still decodes. _planner_loop flushes a pending action only when the next action line (or stream end) arrives, so it can attach a trailing expect. The first action of every turn therefore waits for the whole second line.
